graphicEarnsIt.says: An audio waveform of the film's own soundtrack, with five tall lime bars picked out of the grey amplitude bars and a white playhead line among them. It shows WHERE the cuts fall relative to the audio: five cuts sitting on five transient peaks, evenly spaced. It encodes timing alignment, a quantity (5) and a proportion (which peaks are cut points versus which are just loud), and it proves the claim 'on the beat' rather than asserting it. RIGHT's frame at the same moment encodes nothing; it is type on a gradient.

An audio waveform of the film's own soundtrack with five loud onsets picked out in lime and a playhead riding one of them, labelled beat.wav and '5 cuts, 5 beats'. It shows a count and an alignment: the film contains exactly five cuts, and each one sits on a peak in the audio rather than on an arbitrary frame. The quieter grey bars around the marked ones give the claim its evidence, because you can see the marked spikes are the tall ones. RIGHT's version of this beat encodes nothing; it is the assertion in type with a glow behind it.

An audio waveform with five tall bright markers standing above the noise floor: it shows that five cuts in the film sit exactly on five loud beats of the track, so the timing claim 'on the beat' is measured rather than asserted. The one thin white marker reads as the current playhead against those five hits. RIGHT has no picture at all in any beat, only type on a gradient.
